newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on diminished frost concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on diminished frost concerns.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on diminished fears about frost damage to the U.S. corn crop, traders said.
"We're just putting weather premium in, then taking it out...back and forth," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

The market ended firm Thursday on a report of potential frost by September 23 or September 24 in northern areas of the U.S. Midwest, including northern Iowa. But early on Friday, weather maps indicated diminished chances of such cold weather soon in key U.S. corn/soy states.
"Today's version (of the maps) does not infer a freeze on the (September 23 or 24)," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.
Dean Witter Reynolds sold four million bushels of December, Cargill Inc sold four million December and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold five million March, traders said.
Corn futures closed 3-1/2 to 8-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 3-1/2 at $3.61-3/4. December closed 8-1/2 lower at $3.21-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 40,000, down from 51,649 Thursday.
Corn options trading was active with commercial buying of calls noted, the traders said.

Continental Grain bought 500 December $4.00 calls at one cent and bought 1,000 December $3.80 calls at 1-3/4 cents, the traders said. Smith Barney bought 2,000 May $3.70 calls and sold 2,000 puts at even money, sources said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000, up from 16,665 Thursday.
